'''Ashwani Pareek''' (born 27 September 1969 in  [[Delhi]] and native of [[Sambhar Salt Lake|Sambhar Lake]], [[Rajasthan]], [[India]]) is Executive Director of NABI<ref>[https://nabi.res.in/profile/scientists?id=MTA%3D Scientists] nabi.res.in {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210109070059/https://nabi.res.in/profile/scientists?id=MTA%3D |date=9 January 2021 }}</ref> a prominent [[botany|plant biologist]]<ref>Scholar profile of Prof Ashwani Pareek on Samviti.com https://www.samviti.com/profile/ashwani-pareek-NzM4</ref><ref name="auto2">Visitors Award 2018 for the Best Technology https://jnu.ac.in/sites/default/files/Pareek_Award%20.pdf</ref> and [[teacher|educator]] noted chiefly for his contribution in [[molecular biology|plant molecular biology]] and [[biotechnology]]. He is currently working as Professor of [[molecular biology|plant molecular biology]] and [[biotechnology]] at the School of Life Sciences, [[Jawaharlal Nehru University|Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi]],<ref>Home page, Ashwani Pareek https://jnu.ac.in/content/ashwanip</ref> and [[adjunct professor]] at the [[University of Western Australia|University of Western Australia, Perth, Australia]].<ref name="auto1">, Ashwani Pareek, Adjunct Professor, UWA https://research-repository.uwa.edu.au/en/persons/ashwani-pareek</ref> He is a recipient of several honors including the Visitors award for Technology Development from the [[President of India]] for developing Stress Tolerant Rice of the Next Generation (STRONG)<ref name="auto">Visitor’s award for research and technology development https://presidentofindia.nic.in/press-release-detail.htm?1324</ref><ref name="auto2"/> that has the potential to enhance the income of rice farmers. The award ceremony was held at the [[Rashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi|Rashtrapati Bhawan]] on 2 May 2018. Recently on 26 February 2020, he has been awarded "Tata Innovation Award 2020" by [[Department of Biotechnology|Department of Biotechnology, Govt of India]].<ref>TATA Innovation fellowship
2019-20 http://dbtindia.gov.in/sites/default/files/Selected%20Tata%20Innovation%20Fellows%202019-20.pdf</ref><ref>Ashwani Pareek, receives Tata Innovation Award 2020 by DBT, GoI
https://jnu.ac.in/content/jnu-achievements</ref> He has interest in understanding the physiological and molecular adaptations in xero-halophytic plants and development of [[transgenic plants|transgenic rice plants]] with enhanced tolerance towards multiple [[abiotic stress]]es.

==Education and professional career==
Pareek received bachelor's degree (1987-1990) in [[botany]] and master's degree (1990-1992) in [[molecular biology|plant molecular biology]] from the [[University of Delhi]]. He then joined the laboratory of Professor [[Anil Grover]] at the same university in 1992 for [[Doctor of Philosophy|doctoral research (PhD)]] work on ‘Molecular Characterization of stress proteins in ''Oryza sativa'' L. with emphasis on 90 kDa family’.

After receiving [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] degree, Pareek received the prestigious Post Doctoral Fellowship by The [[Rockefeller Foundation|Rockefeller Foundation, New York]] and worked with Professor Ralph S.Quatrano at the [[University of North Carolina|University of North Carolina, USA]] during 1997–98. He then accepted the assignment of research scientist at Department of Genetics, [[University of Delhi]] South Campus in late 1998. In May, 2001, Pareek was awarded BOYSCAST Fellowship to work with Professor Hans Bohnert at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign|University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign, US]]. Thereafter in 2005, he was awarded the INSA-Royal visiting scientist fellowship to work at University of Cambridge, UK. Pareek joined Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2003 and presently serving there as a professor of plant molecular biology. In 2012, he was conferred the DBT-Overseas visiting fellowship(CREST) to work at The University of California, Davis, US.<ref>Prestigious awards and fellowships to Ashwani Pareek http://naasindia.org/detail.php?id=331</ref> In 2017, he was appointed as adjunct professor at the University of Western Australia, Perth, Australia.<ref name="auto1"/>

==Research publications and books==

Ashwani has authored and published more than 150 research papers/articles in the research journals.<ref>Ashwani Pareek- Google SCholar https://scholar.google.co.in/citations?user=l8ux08UAAAAJ&hl=en</ref> Some of these journals include [[Nature (journal)|Nature]], [[Journal of Experimental Botany]], [[Plant Physiology (journal)|Plant Physiology]], [[The Plant Journal]], [[Plant, Cell & Environment]] etc. He has edited/ co-edited three books like ‘Abiotic Stress Adaptation in Plants: Physiological, Molecular and Genomic Foundation’,<ref>Abiotic Stress Adaptation in Plants https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9789048131112</ref> ‘Biotechnology in Medicine and Agriculture: Principles and Practices’.<ref>Biotechnology in Medicine and Agriculture https://www.ikbooks.com/books/book/life-sciences/biotechnology/biotechnology-medicine-agriculture/9789381141403/</ref> and ‘Pre-Field Screening Protocols for Heat Tolerant Mutants in Rice’.<ref>Pre-Field Screening Protocols for Heat-Tolerant Mutants in Rice https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9783319773377</ref>
